findings.message: packages/simulation/src/objectives/property.test.ts economyCheck (lines 125-137): the per-step 'at most one tonic is active' check only asserts that the single tonicEffect slot is null or spans tonicTicks. That holds by construction for any state useTonic can produce, so it would still pass if an activation overwrote a still-active tonic (burning a carried tonic). The 'tonic-active' stat at line 335 is only counted, never asserted per step. The behaviour is still guarded by the scripted test 'allows one active at a time, and another once it ends' (ledger.test.ts, rejections at ticks 10 and 249) and by EXERCISED requiring at least one use-tonic:tonic-active. But the per-step property itself cannot fail on stacking. A real per-step check would assert that a successful use-tonic found no active tonic for that player in the prior state.
findings.requirement: After every step: the invariant holds, no gold goes negative, the tonic count is between 0 and 2, and at most one tonic is active.

findings.message: The scripted duel refusals for purchase ('refuses when gold is short, in a duel, ...') and useTonic ('is refused in a duel, off the sea, ...') in ledger.test.ts only reserve a duel and test during the 'fighting' phase. No scripted test covers the 'choosing' window, where both players stay reserved (docs/objectives.md). activeDuelOf (state.ts:351) covers it, and the property run's buy-*:player-in-duel / use-tonic:player-in-duel counts may include it, but no deterministic assertion does.
findings.requirement: - It is refused when gold is short, when the player is in a duel (reserved) or has left, or, for a tonic, when the player already carries two.
